newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rates ease.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rates ease.

text.p: Money market rates eased on Tuesday amid dwindling demand as most banks replenished their accounts after three days of being relatively short.
"We can breathe easier now, but it is difficult to say how long this is going to last," one dealer said.
Fresh morning deals totalled 30.3 million kuna, about half of which was call money at 10.5 percent, down from yesterday's weighted 10.68 percent rate.
"Better supply immediately stabilised the price of call-money," said the dealer.
Supply was stronger with 23 million kuna in surplus. However demand of some five million was not met as some clients had already exceeded a debt limit set by creditors.
Term loans, totalling 10 million kuna, varied between 11 and 15 percent for two-week and one-month money, while two-month deals were made at 15 and 18 percent, the latter borrowed by a savings bank.
Overnight trade amounted to 60 million kuna taken by two banks to maintain their mandatory reserves.
The central bank granted five million kuna in new lombard funds at 9.5 percent. It had 142.6 million kuna in outstanding loans by the end of Monday, an official said.
